policy.title: Sign-up policy
policy.description: Decide who can sign up and how. Only system administrators can change this, and every change is audited.
policy.enabledBody: When off, nobody can create a new account from the sign-up page. Existing accounts keep signing in.
policy.domains: Email domains allowed to sign up
policy.domainsBody: Leave empty to let anyone sign up. If set, only those domains can sign up.
policy.activationSubtitle: With both on, email verification comes first, then admin approval.
policy.verifyBody: The account activates after the 6-digit code sent to the email is entered.
policy.approvalBody: The account activates after a system administrator approves it in Accounts.
policy.noGateWarning: Both requirements are off, so new accounts activate immediately.
policy.ratePerIp: Sign-up requests per IP per hour
policy.teamGrantDefault: Default count when allowing team workspaces
policy.teamGrantDefaultHelp: Signed-up accounts cannot create team workspaces. Allow them per account in Accounts.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.description: Approve sign-ups, suspend or restore accounts, and allow team workspace creation. Every account lives in Keycloak; approval and suspension apply there immediately.

approve.label: Approve
approve.title: Approve {{name}}?
approve.body: They can sign in right away, and their personal workspace is created.

reject.label: Reject
reject.title: Reject {{name}}'s sign-up?
reject.body: This account won't be able to sign in.

suspend.label: Suspend
suspend.title: Suspend {{name}}?
suspend.body: Their next request is blocked and they can't sign in. Their data stays as it is.

teamLimit.title: {{name}} — creating team workspaces
teamLimit.body: Set how many team workspaces this account can create. 0 means none. It has created {{created}} so far.
teamLimit.label: Allowed count
teamLimit.help: If you set fewer than already created, existing workspaces stay and no more can be created.
teamLimit.saved: {{name}} can now create up to {{limit}} team workspaces.
teamLimit.savedNone: {{name}} can no longer create team workspaces.

accounts.leftoverMembershipsHint: This account used workspaces before it became a system admin. It can no longer enter them but is still listed as a member. Use a dedicated account for system administration: remove the role from this account or remove it from the workspaces.
accounts.teamsSystemAdminHint: System admin accounts cannot create or join workspaces

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.description: See every workspace's name, address, owner, member count and status. Content (projects, issues) is not visible here. Team workspaces can be suspended and resumed, and can only be deleted after they are suspended. Every action is audited.
workspaces.emptySearch: No workspace matches that name or address
workspaces.personalHintLong: A personal workspace belongs to its account and is not suspended or deleted on its own. To block that person, suspend the account in Accounts.

suspend.title: Suspend {{name}}
suspend.body: From the next request, no member (owners included) can use this workspace's screens, REST or MCP, and they see a suspended notice. MCP keys no longer reach it. Data, members and roles stay, and everything comes back when you resume it.
suspend.reasonHelp: Kept only in system admin screens and the audit log. Members don't see it. (Up to 500 characters)

resume.title: Resume {{name}}
resume.body: From the next request, members can use it exactly as before the suspension. MCP keys reach it again.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}
delete.warning: This can't be undone. The Keycloak organization (memberships, roles) and attachment files are deleted, along with members, roles, invitations, join requests, issue templates and notifications. Projects, issues and history become invisible to everyone and are purged after the retention period. The audit log stays.
delete.confirmLabel: To confirm, type the address {{slug}} exactly
delete.notSuspended: Only suspended workspaces can be deleted.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Skills are instructions that external agents (such as Claude Code) download with the MCP tool get_skill. Only system admins add, edit and delete them; every change adds a revision and an audit record. Agents follow this text as is, so check it carefully before you change it.
skills.emptyBody: Create a skill or import a SKILL.md, and agents can download it over MCP.
skills.notFoundBody: The name is wrong or the skill does not exist.

delete.title: Delete the skill {{name}}?
delete.body: It disappears from the list and from MCP (list_skills · get_skill), so agents can no longer download it. Its revisions are kept, and you can restore it at any time.
delete.done: Deleted the skill {{name}}. You can restore it.

import.title: Import SKILL.md
import.body: Pick or paste a Claude Code skill file (frontmatter name · description plus the body). If no skill has that name, a new one is created. If one exists, you are asked once, and that skill is edited with this content (a new revision).
import.exists: The skill {{name}} (revision {{no}}) already exists. To edit it with this content, choose "Edit with this content".

form.nameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 64 characters (e.g. moai-works-issues). It cannot be changed later.
form.nameFixed: The name cannot be changed after the skill is created.
form.name_tooLong: The name can be up to 64 characters.
form.name_pattern: Use only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (no hyphen at either end, no double hyphens).
form.descriptionHelp: Agents read this to decide when to use the skill. Say clearly which requests it is for.
form.descriptionTooLong: The description can be up to {{max}} characters.
form.bodyPlaceholder: Write the instructions for agents in Markdown.
form.bodyHelp: Markdown (up to 100,000 characters). Agents read it as instructions. Control characters other than newline and tab are rejected.
form.noteHelp: Agents read this when they download the new revision of the skill, to learn what changed. Say what you changed and why in {{min}}–{{max}} characters. It is also shown in the revision timeline and the audit log.
form.noteHelpCreate: If left empty, "처음 만듦" (first version) is recorded. Agents read this when they first download the skill. It is also shown in the revision timeline and the audit log.
form.notePlaceholder: e.g. Added the on-hold and cancelled statuses and their reason rule
form.note_required: Enter a summary of changes of at least {{min}} characters — agents read it to learn what changed.
form.note_tooLong: The summary of changes can be up to {{max}} characters.
form.conflictBody: This form can no longer be saved. Copy your changes somewhere, reload, and edit again.
form.deletedBody: Deleted skills cannot be edited. Restore it first.

view.deletedNotice: {{name}} deleted this skill at {{time}}. It is hidden from the list and from MCP. Its revisions are kept; restore it to show it again.

revisions.emptyBody: Every time the skill is created or edited, a revision is added.
revisions.diffSummary: Revision {{from}} → revision {{to}} · items changed: {{fields}} · body lines added: {{added}} · removed: {{removed}}
revisions.reversed: You are comparing in reverse: revision {{from}} is newer than revision {{to}}.
revisions.fieldsEmpty: The name and description are the same.
revisions.coarse: Too much changed to match line by line. It is shown as all old lines removed and all new lines added.

restoreRevision.title: Revert to revision {{no}}?
restoreRevision.body: The description and body of {{name}} become those of revision {{no}}, as a new revision {{next}}. All earlier revisions are kept. Agents get this content from their next download.
restoreRevision.notePlaceholder: e.g. Back to the rules of revision {{no}}
restoreRevision.done: Created revision {{no}} with the content of revision {{from}}.
restoreRevision.conflict: Someone else edited it in the meantime. Reload and revert again.
restoreRevision.unchanged: It matches the current content, so no new revision was created.
